- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.6) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast peak values by 2–5%.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.4) or volatile, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 2–5% to compensate for downward bias.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast peak at 10–15% above recent high.
- If sentiment shifts from positive to negative mid-horizon, model fails to adjust; reduce forecast slope downward by 1–2% per sentiment drop.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon; if forecast is >10% above 30-day moving average, reduce by 1–3% per day until convergence.
- If sentiment history shows high volatility (alternating 0.2–0.8), model overfits short-term noise; smooth forecast with 3-day moving average filter.
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome is consistently below model (e.g., 5–10% gap), model is biased upward; apply downward correction proportional to sentiment negativity.
